title: Foreign intervention in the Spanish Civil War
stem: Paper 2 essay practice on the causes and effects of 20th-century wars. Plan for about 45 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: To what extent was foreign intervention the main reason for the Nationalist victory in the Spanish Civil War?
markscheme: Introduction with a clear thesis weighing foreign intervention against other factors
German aid: airlift of the Army of Africa (1936), Condor Legion, Guernica (1937), tactics and equipment
Italian aid: tens of thousands of CTV troops, aircraft and supplies
Non-Intervention Committee: Britain and France denied the Republic legal arms purchases
Soviet aid to the Republic declined and was paid for with Spanish gold; International Brigades limited militarily
Nationalist unity: Franco's single command and the 1937 unification of Falange and Carlists
Republican divisions: anarchists, communists, POUM; May Days in Barcelona (1937)
Military factors: professional officers and the Army of Africa versus militias; Battle of the Ebro (1938)
Support from the Church, landowners and conservative regions
Conclusion: reasoned judgement, e.g. intervention was decisive in 1936 but Republican disunity and Nationalist unity explain the outcome by 1939
parts.notes: Real essays are marked out of 15 with markbands; this practice version uses a 10-point checklist. Avoid narrative: every paragraph should weigh the factor's importance.
